title: Check yourself: what field 39 asks of whom

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: A taxi's card reader asks the issuer for 42.00 on a prepaid card. The response has field 39 = 10, and the amount in it is 30.00. What should the reader do?

options.text: Treat the 42.00 fare as paid, since 10 is one of the codes an issuer uses for an approval
options.says: 10 approves only part of the amount; read as a full approval, the driver is paid 30.00 for a 42.00 fare

options.text: Treat the 42.00 fare as unpaid, since 30.00 is the balance the issuer reports with a decline
options.says: 10 is an approval for part of the amount, not a decline; read as a decline, the issuer holds 30.00 that no fare uses

options.text: Ask the passenger to pay the other 12.00 another way, since the issuer approved 30.00 of the fare
options.says: a partial approval covers part of the amount, and the rest is collected some other way

options.text: Ask the issuer to approve the full 42.00 in a new request, since a second request may cover the whole fare
options.says: the issuer approved what the card could pay; asking again for the full amount finds nothing more to give, and the rest is collected some other way

origin.section: 9.1. Several Codes Approve, and a Partial Approval Covers Only Part of the Amount

questions.stem: An ATM gets 55 for a withdrawal and, to be safe, sends the withdrawal once more with a new STAN and the same PIN block. The issuer blocks a card after three wrong PINs. What has the second request done?

options.text: It counts as a second wrong PIN, since the issuer checks the PIN block again and finds the same PIN
options.says: the same request gets the same decision, and each wrong PIN the issuer checks counts toward its limit

options.text: It counts as a fresh chance, since a 55 is often a passing fault that a second request clears
options.says: 55 is the issuer's decision about the PIN, not a fault; only the right PIN changes it

options.text: It changes nothing, since the issuer sees the same PIN block and repeats its earlier answer unchecked
options.says: with a new STAN it is a new request, and the issuer checks its PIN like any other

options.text: It changes nothing, since only a cardholder typing a PIN at the keypad counts as a try
options.says: the issuer counts the wrong PINs it checks; it cannot tell who produced the PIN block

origin.section: 9.2. A Decline Is Final for Its Request, and Its Code Says Who Could Change the Answer

questions.stem: On Monday morning, after a release of the acquirer's software, a supermarket's purchases come back with 30, one after another. The tills show "declined, try another card". What follows?

options.text: Cardholders try other cards, and those come back 30 too, since the message itself is wrong
options.says: 30 is a format error in the sender's message; any card fails the same way until a developer fixes the mapping

options.text: Cardholders try other cards, and those are approved, since 30 concerned the first card only
options.says: 30 reports a failure of the message, not a decision about the card

options.text: Nobody is affected for long, since the till sends each refused purchase again a minute later
options.says: the same message sent again unchanged fails again; the mapping has to be fixed

options.text: Nobody is affected for long, since the issuer adjusts its checks after the first refused purchase
options.says: the error is in the sender's message; the receiver does not change to accept it

origin.section: 9.3. An Error Code Reports a Failure, Not a Decision About the Card

questions.stem: A reversal sender treats every action code whose first digit is not 0 as a failure. It is connected to a processor that answers with four-digit action codes, and every reversal is answered 4000. What happens to the reversals?

options.text: Each is sent until the limit and parked, since the sender takes the processor's 4000 for a refusal
options.says: 4000 accepts a reversal; a sender that treats every code outside 0 as a failure keeps resending a reversal the receiver applied, then parks it

options.text: Each is sent until the limit and parked, since 4000 means the processor found no original to undo
options.says: 4000 is the code for an accepted reversal, not for a missing original

options.text: Each leaves the queue at the first answer, since 4000 starts with the digit of the reversal category
options.says: the sender looks only at whether the first digit is 0; 4000 fails that test, so it keeps resending

options.text: Each leaves the queue at the first answer, since a sender built for 1987 reads 4000 as 00
options.says: nothing translates the code; a sender that treats every code outside 0 as a failure keeps resending an acknowledged reversal

origin.section: 9.4. Later Editions Put the Category in the First Digit

concepts: A decline is final for its request: resending gets the same answer, a resent wrong PIN counts again, and the code says whether the cardholder, the merchant or a phone call could change the outcome.

Error codes report a failure rather than a decision about the card: 30, 12 and 13 point at the sender's message, 91 and 96 at the other side's systems, 63 at the keys, and a missing code decides nothing.
In the later editions and jPOS's CMF the first digit of the action code names its category, and acceptances such as 4000, 8000 and 9001 lie outside category 0.
More than one code approves (00, 08, 10, 11, and 85 for a verification), and 10 approves only part of the amount, so the rest is collected another way.
